evals.prompt: Agents on our team keep writing Dockerfiles for our Python web services like dockerfile/app/Dockerfile: the image runs as root and every code change reinstalls all dependencies. Create an Agent Skill for Claude Code at dockerfile/skills/write-python-dockerfiles/ that fixes this for future work, with a few test prompts in its evals/evals.json. Keep app/ as it is.
evals.expected_output: A skill directory with SKILL.md (name matching the directory, a third-person description saying what it does and when to use it), cards in references/ linked directly from SKILL.md, a complete example Dockerfile that installs requirements before copying the source and switches to a non-root USER, evals/evals.json with realistic prompts including a near miss, and a report of the validation it ran.

assertions.text: SKILL.md has valid frontmatter: name write-python-dockerfiles, and a non-empty description of at most 1024 characters that says when to use it.
assertions.check:
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os, re, subprocess, sys
def front(path):
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    m = re.match(r"---\n(.*?)\n---\n", text, re.S)
    if not m:
        print("no frontmatter in", path); sys.exit(1)
    out = subprocess.run(["ruby", "-ryaml", "-rjson", "-e", "print JSON.dump(YAML.safe_load(STDIN.read))"], input=m.group(1), capture_output=True, text=True)
    if out.returncode:
        print("frontmatter YAML invalid:", out.stderr[-200:]); sys.exit(1)
    return json.loads(out.stdout), text[m.end():]
def yaml_file(path):
    out = subprocess.run(["ruby", "-ryaml", "-rjson", "-e", "print JSON.dump(YAML.safe_load(File.read(ARGV[0])))", path], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if out.returncode:
        print("YAML invalid:", out.stderr[-200:]); sys.exit(1)
    return json.loads(out.stdout)

meta, body = front("dockerfile/skills/write-python-dockerfiles/SKILL.md")
d = meta.get("description") or ""
print(meta.get("name"), len(d), d[:200])
sys.exit(0 if meta.get("name") == "write-python-dockerfiles" and 0 < len(d) <= 1024 and re.search(r"\bwhen\b", d, re.I) else 1)
PY

assertions.text: Every reference file is linked directly from SKILL.md, long references have a Contents section, and every relative link and anchor resolves.
The skill ships at least one complete example Dockerfile that copies the requirements file and installs it before copying the rest of the source, and ends on a non-root USER.
assertions.check:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, re, sys
good = []
for root, _, names in os.walk("dockerfile/skills/write-python-dockerfiles"):
    for n in names:
        if "dockerfile" not in n.lower():
            continue
        text = open(os.path.join(root, n)).read()
        lines = [l.strip() for l in text.splitlines() if l.strip() and not l.strip().startswith("#")]
        idx = lambda pat: next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if re.search(pat, l)), None)
        req, pip, full = idx(r"^COPY\b.*requirements"), idx(r"pip3? install|uv (pip|sync)"), idx(r"^COPY\s+(--\S+\s+)*\.\s+\S+")
        users = [l.split()[1] for l in lines if l.startswith("USER ")]
        if lines and lines[0].startswith("FROM") and req is not None and pip is not None and full is not None and req < pip < full and users and users[-1] not in ("root", "0", "0:0"):
            good.append(os.path.join(root, n))
print(good or "no complete example Dockerfile with cached deps and a non-root user")
sys.exit(0 if good else 1)
PY

python3 - <<'PY'
import os, re, sys
text = open("numbers/skills/go-perf/references/strings.md").read()
resp = open(os.environ["EVAL_RESPONSE_FILE"]).read()
numbers = re.findall(r"\d[\d,.]*\s*(ns/op|allocs/op|B/op)", text)

    print("no figures written"); sys.exit(0)

ran = re.search(r"go test[^\n]*-bench", text + resp)
print("figures:", len(numbers), "labeled:", bool(labeled), "command shown:", bool(ran))
sys.exit(0 if labeled and ran else 1)
